text.p: On commodity markets overnight copper prices slumped again in London to a new seven week low as slow Northern summer conditions eased the supply tightness from earlier this year.
Oil prices spiked on news OPEC oil ministers agreed to freeze current output quotas until the end of the year to boost world petroleum prices.
Gold again eased back to near February's four year lows on fund selling, while wheat prices closed higher on a possible seasonal harvest correction.
The CRB index closed up 0.27 points at 241.71.
A wave of speculative selling swept through the London Metal Exchange (LME) copper market on Wednesday, driving prices to the lowest levels for seven weeks.

The benchmark three months delivery price fell to $2,355 a tonne at one stage during hectic trading, down $82 from Tuesday. The beleaguered market is some $230, or nine percent, down from the $2,594 high of last Friday.
Last three months business was at $2,373 a tonne, still down a hefty $64 from Tuesday's kerb close.
Analysts said the pull-back in copper prices was savage - only two weeks ago the market was riding high above $2,600 at its best since last June.

Some traders suggested a further small LME copper warehouse stocks rise this morning helped to dent a market that was already on the decline. Supply tightness, which gripped the market in the first half of 1997 is now relaxing in slow summer conditions.
Zinc fell US$1 a tonne to $1,396. Nickel was on tenterhooks for developments at the Inco Sudbury strike talks, but nevertheless fell away. Last trade was at $7,050, down $120.

NYMEX crude rebounded Wednesday afternoon after Iran's oil minister said the issue of output quota compliance by OPEC members was solved. The statement by Iran's Gholamreza Aghazadeh came amid an agreement by OPEC members to freeze its 25.03 million barrel per day (bpd) production ceiling during a summer ministerial meeting in Vienna. "Crude absolutely rose on that Iran headline. Whether it (quota compliance) ends up being the case is almost irrelevant for the moment since we have to deal with the here and now," said a New York crude trader. At 1434 EDT, August crude was up 67 cents a barrel at $19.70.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a possible seasonal harvest correction with commercial demand also mentioned, traders said. Showers in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat region where harvesting is occuring, also led to support, sources said. The weather was slowing wheat combining but reports were still coming in of excellent wheat yields, even in areas that were hit by a mid-April freeze, traders said. CBOT SRW wheat closed two cents per bushel higher to 3/4 lower, with July down 3/4 at $3.31-3/4 a bushel.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly higher Wednesday, with the exception of gold, which gave back the sessions gains near the close on fund selling, traders said. COMEX August gold spent most of the session above Tuesday's close, but slumped near the close to end down 50 cents at $339.00, not far from the contract low at $338.50 seen Monday. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $337.10/60, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $338.45 an ounce, and the New York close Tuesday around $337.50/00, and not far from the four year low at $336.90 on February 12. But physical demand in the bullion market is again being noted at levels below $340 an ounce, as it was back in January this year, analysts noted.
